question: Are Bryant Peak North Route and West Face real routes?
answer: Not established. Rock-wise Bryant (5,801 ft) has only the southwest ridge/Hemlock Pass scramble; the north/west sides appear as ice (Hot Tubbs WI4-, My Condolences WI2+, a winter Northeast Face WI3) and approach corridors via Source Lake/Bryant Col. A '5.2 West Face' is not documented anywhere; the stored 5.2 looks unsupported. A single logged ascent named 'West Face' was in March (likely winter ice/snow, not rock).
recommendation: Delete wa_bryant_peak_north_route (no content, no source). For West Face: delete too, unless the owner knows its first-ascent line; if kept, clear the 5.2 grade. If a winter Northeast Face row is wanted it is a separate new row (ice WI3, ~4 pitches, Source Lake approach), not these.
evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryant_Peak — easiest route scramble, no named north/west routes
